What's in your set

Every set is drawn from your answers, for your job and your township. Pick your project to see what you'll get.

A complete sample new-home set, sheet by sheet, drawn like our full builder sets. Tap any sheet to see it full size.

  1. A0.0

    Cover sheet and site plan

    Sheet index, project data and codes for your ZIP code. The site plan shows your lot, setbacks, driveway, utilities and spot elevations. Open items are listed in red.

    Drawn from your answers in sections A and C.

  2. A0.1

    General notes, code data and schedules

    Code notes, design criteria for your township, and the window and door schedules tied to tags on the plans.

    Drawn from your answers in sections A, E and F.

  3. A0.3

    Excavation and grading plan

    Existing and finished grades from county GIS, FEMA and EGLE data, dig limits and depth, stockpiles, silt fence and drainage.

    Drawn from your answers in sections A and C.

  4. A0.6

    Fill and grading plan

    Color map of fill depth around the house, finished contours, spot grades, design elevations and fill sand quantities to order.

    Drawn from your answers in sections A, C and E.

  5. A1.0

    Foundation plan

    Footings, walls, flush girder, columns, slabs, the sump pit and every sleeve through the foundation, all dimensioned.

    Drawn from your answers in sections E and H.

  6. A1.1

    Floor plan

    Every room named and sized, with full dimension strings, door swings, and window and door tags.

    Drawn from your answers in sections B, D, G and I.

  7. A1.2

    Roof plan

    Ridges, valleys, pitches and overhangs, with flashing, ice barrier, attic ventilation and roof areas for ordering.

    Drawn from your answers in sections D and E.

  8. A2.1

    Exterior elevations

    Each side with siding, roofing and trim called out, floor, plate and ridge heights, and an exterior materials schedule.

    Drawn from your answers in sections E and F.

  9. A3.1

    Building section

    A cut from footing to ridge that labels every layer: foundation, floor system, walls, insulation and roof.

    Drawn from your answers in section E.

  10. P1.1

    Plumbing rough-in

    Every fixture where you want it, with a fixture schedule, drain routing, stacks, the water heater and hose bibs.

    Drawn from your answers in sections H and I.

  11. E1.1

    Electrical plan

    Lights, switches, outlets, alarms and garage door opener buttons, with switches at every entry along your walking path.

    Drawn from your answers in section G.

  12. A5.1

    Exterior renderings

    The house in 3D from every side, each corner and above, with your siding, roof and trim colors, so owners see it before it is built.

    Drawn from your answers in section F.

  13. A0.4Add-on

    Finish plan and schedule

    Flooring by room with transitions, wall finish keys on every wall (paint, tile, shiplap, wainscot), and a room finish schedule.

    Drawn from your answers in section Q.

  14. A1.3Add-on

    Reflected ceiling plan

    Ceiling types and heights room by room: tray, tongue-and-groove, beams, soffits and drywall, with a ceiling schedule.

    Drawn from your answers in section Q.

  15. A4.7Add-on

    Trim, counter and cabinet details

    Countertop plan with overhangs and seams, kitchen elevation, trim profiles and countertop edge sections.

    Drawn from your answers in sections I and Q.

Also with every set

  • The complete set as a PDF, ready to print or upload to your township
  • Code references for your township and ZIP code
  • Site elevations from county GIS, FEMA and EGLE maps for additions and new homes, marked "verify by survey"
  • Anything we couldn't confirm marked in red and listed on the cover, never guessed
  • A revision block that logs every change after delivery
  • Homeowners: a budget price range for the project, if you ask for one

Permit drawings, not engineering. BL Plans sets are not licensed architectural or engineering drawings, and we don't provide engineering. If your township or your project needs an engineer's seal, you'll hire one, and we'll coordinate the drawings with their design.

Commercial work, or a project that doesn't fit these? Describe it in the form and we'll tell you which sheets it needs before you pay anything.

What to expect

From the form to your permit, here's every step and who does it.

Start a job
  1. You

    Fill out the form

    Answer the questions below and upload sketches, plans, photos or a 3D scan. Skip anything you don't know.

  2. BL Plans

    We review your job

    We check every answer, look up the lot, flood and wetland maps and site elevations, and find the codes for your township and ZIP code. If something's missing, we call you.

  3. You

    Pay your invoice

    We email a flat-fee invoice for your project type. For builder pricing, we verify your Michigan license first. Drawing starts once the invoice is paid.

  4. BL Plans

    We draw your set

    Every sheet your permit needs, drawn from your answers. Anything we can't confirm is marked in red for you to verify. Average turnaround is 3 to 5 business days for decks, remodels, basements, garages and pole barns, 5 to 7 for additions and 7 to 10 for new homes.

  5. You

    Review your set

    We email you the PDF. Check every sheet, and verify dimensions and existing conditions in the field.

  6. You

    Ask for changes, if you need any

    Each change after delivery is a flat fee, paid before we make it. We log it on the revision block and send the updated set.

  7. You

    Submit for your permit

    Print the set or upload it to your township. Then build.

Start your job

Talk it through

Tap the mic and describe the job the way you would on the phone: what you're building, the size, the rooms, what stays and what's new, and the materials. Add your name, company, phone, email and the job address. We'll fill in what we can. Then check the highlighted answers and finish the rest.

      LBuilder responsibilities and sign-off

      By submitting, the builder agrees to the following:

      1. The information in this form and its attachments is accurate and complete. BL Plans relies on it and is not responsible for errors or omissions caused by inaccurate or incomplete information.
      2. Dimensions taken from photos, sketches or scans are approximate. The builder will verify all dimensions, elevations and existing conditions in the field before ordering materials or starting work, and will report any discrepancy to BL Plans in writing before proceeding.
      3. The builder will review the drawings before submitting them for permit and before building. The builder is responsible for construction means and methods, job-site safety, and compliance with all codes, ordinances, manufacturer instructions and permit conditions. Building department approval does not change this.
      4. The drawings are permit drawings. They are not licensed architectural or engineering drawings, and they are not prepared, sealed or reviewed by a licensed architect or professional engineer. BL Plans does not provide engineering. Engineered products such as trusses and LVL, PSL or I-joist members are designed by their manufacturer. Where engineering is required, the builder will obtain it from a Michigan-licensed engineer.
      5. BL Plans does not visit the site or observe construction unless agreed in writing. Changes to the drawings by others, or construction that departs from them, are the responsibility of the party who makes them.
      6. To the fullest extent permitted by law, BL Plans' total liability for any claim relating to the drawings is limited to the fee paid for them.
      7. The drawings are for this job only and remain the property of BL Plans. They may not be reused or shared without written permission.
      8. Builder pricing requires a current Michigan residential builder or maintenance and alteration license, which BL Plans verifies with the State of Michigan. If the license can't be verified, or doesn't match the company submitting, homeowner pricing applies.
      9. The fee is set by project type: $399 for a deck, porch, remodel, basement finish, garage or pole barn; $699 for an addition; $999 for a new home; commercial work is quoted. The interior finish package add-on is $30 and the logo add-on is $15. Each change the builder requests after the set is delivered is billed at $50. All fees are paid in full before work begins: the set before drawing starts, and each change before it is made.
      10. Any material list provided with the drawings is an estimate for convenience only. The builder will verify every quantity, size, grade and product against the approved drawings, field conditions and supplier requirements before ordering. BL Plans is not responsible for shortages, overages or ordering errors.

      Common questions

      How long does a set take?

      Average turnaround is 3 to 5 business days for decks, porches, remodels, basement finishes, garages and pole barns, 5 to 7 for additions and 7 to 10 for new homes. The clock starts when your invoice is paid and we have every answer we need. Changes after delivery take 1 to 2 business days.

      What do I get?

      A PDF set on 24 x 36 sheets with every sheet your permit needs, a title block on each sheet, and a cover listing anything still to verify in red. Print it or upload it to your township.

      Are these engineered drawings?

      No. They're permit drawings, not licensed architectural or engineering drawings. Trusses, LVLs and other engineered products are designed by their supplier. If your township requires engineering, for example on a post-frame building or a retaining wall, you hire a Michigan-licensed engineer and we coordinate the drawings with their design.

      Which code do you draw to?

      The Michigan Residential Code edition your township enforces on the day we draw, with its ground snow load, frost depth, wind speed and energy requirements for your ZIP code. We list each value and its source on the general notes sheet.

      Do pole barns have to meet the energy code?

      Only if they're heated. An unheated barn doesn't. If you heat it now, or plan to, the heated part needs insulated walls and roof, an insulated slab edge and air sealing, and we draw it that way.

      What if the township sends back comments?

      Send us the review letter. We'll tell you what each comment needs. Changes to the drawings after delivery are a flat fee each, paid before we make them.

      Do you visit the site?

      No. We draw from your answers, sketches, photos and scans. You verify dimensions and existing conditions in the field before ordering or building.

      Can you do the REScheck and Manual J?

      Yes. Add them in section B7: the REScheck report is $214 and Manual J and S are $286 for builders ($306 and $408 for homeowners). They come with your set, a few business days after the drawings.
